newsitem.title: GERMANY: German public borrowing 60 bln marks in 1998 - paper.
newsitem.headline: German public borrowing 60 bln marks in 1998 - paper.

text.p: A newspaper reported on Friday that Germany expects net borrowing next year to be 60 billion marks, four billion higher than forecast.
In an advance report from Saturday's edition, the daily Berliner Zeitung said its information came from the Finance Ministry. The ministry could not be reached for comment.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel has already said he may increase 1997 borrowing beyond a budgeted 53.4 billion marks. Waigle is under pressure following news that tax revenues are likely to be 18 billion marks below budget this year.

Waigel has whipped up a furore by considering selling some of the government's shares in telecommunications company Deutsche Telekom, or revaluing central bank gold reserves to try to rein in the deficit and ensure Bonn qualifies for European Monetary Union.

But economists say Bonn looks increasingly unlikely to get its budget deficit under three percent of economic output in 1997 -- the figure agreed by EU members as one of the criteria for membership of the single currency from 1999 onwards.

They say failure to cut spending now will mean Bonn also has a tough time getting inside the limit next year -- embarrassing for a country that has preached stability and financial rectitude to its EU partners to ensure the stability of the future currency.

The Berliner Zeitung also said Waigel planned to give ministries more freedom in deciding how to spend their budget allocations in the hope this would cut personnel and materials spending by three percent.
